rows.title_full:
AN ACT RENAMING THE LITERACY COORDINATING COUNCIL TO NATIONAL
LITERACY COUNCIL, STRENGTHENING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS,
EXPANDING ITS MEMBERSHIP STRUCTURE AND SUPPORT MECHANISMS,
AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE
REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7165, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract:
Aims to rename the Literacy Coordinating Council to National Literacy Council to strengthen the powers and functions, as well as expand the membership, structure and support mechanisms of the “Council.”
Mandates the Council to closely coordinate with the Department of Education´s Bureau of Alternate Education (BAE) on programs and projects that are geared towards the universalization of literacy. 
Establishes the Local Literacy Council (LLCs) as support structures at the city, municipal, and barangay levels, which shall serve as the coordinating and advisory body at the local level on matters pertaining to the adoption and implementation of community-based measures for the propagation of literacy.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-03-21, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-03-22 and received by the Senate on 2023-03-22

rows.author: J026;J118;K101;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROCLAIMING THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF PATIENTS, PROVIDING A GRIEVANCE MECHANISM THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Enumerates individual rights of patients as follows:  
Rights to - good quality health care and humane treatment, to dignity, to be informed of his rights and obligations, to choose physician/health institution, to an informed consent, to refuse diagnostic and treatment, to refuse participation in medical research, to religious belief and assistance, to privacy and confidentiality, to disclosure of, and access to information, to correspondence and to receive visitors, to medical records, to health education, to leave against medical advice, and to express grievances.
Provides for societal rights of patients as follows: 
Rights to health, access to quality public health care, healthy and safe workplace, medical information and education programs, participate in policy decisions, access to health facilities, an equitable and economical use of resources, and quality health care in times of insolvency.
Proposes several obligations and responsibilities of patients with regards to his/her medical care and/or personal behavior.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT PROMOTING TRANSPARENT GOVERNANCE AND
INSTITUTING ANTI-CORRUPTION MECHANISMS IN THE OPERATION
OF BANKS AND OTHER FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS,
AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1405, ENTITLED
“AN ACT PROHIBITING DISCLOSURE OF OR INQUIRY INTO, DEPOSITS
WITH ANY BANKING INSTITUTION AND PROVIDING PENALTY
THEREFOR”
rows.title_short:
Promoting Transparent Governance And
Instituting Anti-corruption Mechanisms In The Operation Of Banks And Other Financial Institutions, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 1405, Entitled “ An Act Prohibiting Disclosure Of Or Inquiry Into, Deposits
With Any Banking Institution And Providing Penalty
Therefor”
rows.abstract:
Includes the inquiry or examination made by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), in the exercise of its supervisory powers, as one of the exceptions to the prohibition to examine, inquire or look into deposits, provided that 1.) there is reasonable ground to believe that a fraud, serious irregularity or unlawful activity has been or is being committed by a stockholder, owner, director, trustee, officer or employee of an entity that is subject to the supervision or regulatory power of the BSP and; 2.) it is necessary to look into the deposit to establish such fraud, serious irregularity or unlawful activity.
Provides that inquiry and examination of deposits shall be for the exclusive use of the BSP and shall not be made available to any person or entity, whether public or private, except to the Securities and Exchange Commission, Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation, Anti-Money Laundering Council, Department of Justice, and the courts.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-05-08, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-05-09 and received by the Senate on 2023-05-09

rows.author: J097;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING CORPORATE FARMING AND PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to encourage the private sector in the capitalization of agricultural ventures through a program that will allow firms or partnerships to join into management contracts in producing rice or corn with any farmers´ group (farmers´ associations, cooperatives, and agrarian reform communities (ARCs).
Defines Corporate Farming as the direct ownership or lease of farmland by corporations or partnerships to produce agricultural goods for their employees or the open market.
Proposes several provisions regarding the following: 
a) Corporate Farming Contract or Joint Venture; b) Product Disposition or its Monetary Equivalent; c) Farmers as Project Employees (not less than minimum wage, membership in SSS and PhilHealth; d) Program Administration (DA and DAR as liaison conduit with gov´t agencies); e) Incentive Package ( exemption from customs and duties on the importation of agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizers, agricultural machinery, and other implements; VAT on the importation of agricultural inputs; exemption from capital gains tax who sells/transfers idle agricultural land); f) Other Incentives (loans extended by banks).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2023-03-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMICS AND DEVELOPMENT PLANNING, DEFINING ITS FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Mandates the DEDP to direct the government´s planning and investment programming processes towards sustainable and inclusive economic growth; equitable distribution of opportunities, income, and wealth; and increased productivity.
Tasks the DEDP to prepare and recommend national economic development goals, policies, and programs - monitor their implementation, and shall take over the powers, duties, and functions of the National Economic Development Authority (NEDA).
rows.status: Substituted by HB11199

rows.author: J097;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN ENTERPRISE-BASED EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms among others as follows:
“Enterprise-based education and training program” refers to a practical work-related or workplace-related training program with compulsory related theoretical instructions conducted on the job and implemented within companies, which includes, among others, any of the following modalities:  Apprenticeship, Learnership, On-the-Job Training, Practicum, Work Appreciation Program, Dual Training System, Internship, and In-Company Training.
“Learnership” refers to a practical training, work-based or on-the-job program for approved learnable occupations, for a period not exceeding three (3) months.  Only companies whose learnership programs are approved and registered by the TESDA can hire learners.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2023-03-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING INDUSTRY CLUSTER-BASED PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS THROUGH INTER-LOCAL COOPERATION AND PEOPLE´S PARTICIPATION
rows.abstract:
Declares that the State shall encourage cooperation among LGUs . . . to institutionalize a program to strengthen people's participation in local development, enhance productivity, and guarantee income opportunities for all.

Refers Industry cluster to the geographic concentration of competing but collaborating and independent businesses within a value chain of a broadly defined industry, from suppliers to end products . . .
Proposes, among others - each industry cluster shall formulate an industry plan which shall include:  List of products and services; Activities involved towards products/services' development; Role of each LGU in its development process; Assistance needed from other agencies and institutions; Sources of fund support; Projected income; Areas or gaps that must be addressed; Labor market study for product's development; and Identification of research or studies relevant to the products/services' development from academic institutions.
